intended_object: The weak-form residual at time s of the pressure Poisson equation for forced 3D Navier–Stokes, Δp = −∂ᵢ∂ⱼ(uᵢuⱼ) + div f, tested against a spatial test function ψ: ∫_Ω pΔψ + ∫_Ω Σᵢⱼ uᵢuⱼ∂ᵢ∂ⱼψ + ∫_Ω f·∇ψ. Inferred from the docstring, the name and its use in pressure_slice_identity_ae.
explanation: The body matches the weak pressure-equation residual term by term: p(·,s) is paired with Δψ, uᵢuⱼ with ∂ᵢ∂ⱼψ, and fᵢ with ∂ᵢψ, each integrated over Ω. I checked the signs against the library's weak Navier–Stokes identity, ∫(−u·∂ₜφ − u⊗u:∇φ + ∇u:∇φ − p·div φ − f·φ) = 0. Taking φ = θ(t)∇ψ, the time and viscous terms vanish and what remains is θ times this residual. So the residual vanishing for a.e. s gives exactly the standard identity ∫pΔψ = −∫uᵢuⱼ∂ᵢ∂ⱼψ − ∫f·∇ψ, which is what pressure_slice_identity_ae states. Integrating over Ω rather than ℝ³ is harmless, because the library only uses tests ψ with support in Ω. Working in ℝ³ (Vec3) is the natural setting for the Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg theory, and Mathlib has no general notion this should be built from. One quirk: Ω, u, p and f are implicit arguments that cannot be inferred, so callers always pass them by name. This is a matter of style, not an error.
